newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Fate of Venezuelan airline Viasa to be decided Wed.
newsitem.headline: Fate of Venezuelan airline Viasa to be decided Wed.

text.p: The fate of Venezuela's flag carrier airline Viasa is due to be decided Wednesday in a shareholder's meeting that will see Spanish airline Iberia continue as partner or sell out.
"It all depends on Iberia's position," William Bracho, president of Viasa's labor union, told Reuters.
Bracho said his union was searching with Banque Paribas for investors to inject fresh capital into the struggling company.
"We have a menu of possible options," he said. The meeting is due to start at 1100 local time/1500 GMT.

Viasa faces crippling service charges on some $100 million in debt. Iberia paid $80 million in 1991 for a 40 percent share in the airline. Leading local bank Banco Provincial owns 15 percent and the government the remaining 45 percent.
Viasa has a fleet of some 12 aircraft and 2,200 employees.
